sections.h2: Where is Richmond, VA, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Richmond is the capital of Virginia, built at the fall line of the James River, and it had 226,610 residents at the 2020 census (Wikipedia).

Founded in 1737, Richmond replaced Williamsburg as the capital of the colony in 1780. Its economy runs on law, finance and government, with federal, state and local agencies and banking and legal firms downtown. The median age at the 2020 census was 32.4.

Shockoe Bottom is the low-lying area between Shockoe Hill and Church Hill. Carytown is a commercial strip along Cary Street, the Fan District and Oregon Hill are named neighborhoods, and the East End includes Church Hill, Fulton, Union Hill and Fairmount. Because Richmond is an independent city, one city government assesses, bills and collects the real estate tax, with no county layer.

sections.h2: Which Richmond offices handle real estate tax?
sections.html:
The Office of the Assessor of Real Estate sets values, and the Department of Finance bills and collects the tax.

OfficeRoleContact on the city site
Assessor of Real EstateAssessments and appeals(804) 646-7500, assessmentappeals@rva.gov, City Hall, 900 E. Broad St., Room 802
Department of Finance, Real Estate UnitBilling, collection, relief programs(804) 646-7000 or RVA311.com, 900 E. Broad St.

The assessor's office is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Finance asks residents to send inquiries through the city's RVA 311 system. The city says real estate tax is levied and collected in two billings each year on every $100 of assessed value (Finance real estate page).

sections.h2: When are Richmond real estate taxes due?
sections.html:
Richmond real estate tax is due January 14 for the first half and June 14 for the second half.

The city's important dates page lists January 1 as the date the value of real estate is established, January 14 as the first-half due date and June 14 as the second-half due date. It lists tax escrow documents as due around the same dates. Separately, the city says reassessment notices are mailed on or about July 1 each year with an effective date of value as of July 1, so read the notice you receive for the exact date it uses (important dates).

  • January 14: first half due.
  • June 14: second half due.
  • December 31: the city lists this as the deadline to submit a tax relief application or recertification on its real estate tab.

The city also posts an online penalty and interest waiver request form through RVA 311, and Finance can tell you what applies to your account.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Richmond assessment?
sections.html:
Richmond lists three steps: office review, then the Board of Equalization, then a direct appeal to the court.

The assessor says notices go to each owner's last known address on or about July 1 and show the proposed assessment, prior values and the calculated change in tax. If you have questions, call the assessor's front desk at (804) 646-7500 and talk with the area appraiser before requesting a formal review (appeal process page). The page also lists a tool to determine your residential neighborhood. The notice and the assessor's office will have them.

  • Bring recent comparable sales close to the assessment date.
  • Check the recorded square footage, bedroom count and condition notes.
  • Remember that state law presumes the assessor's value is correct and places the burden on the taxpayer (Va. Code 58.1-3379).

sections.h2: What is Richmond's real estate tax sale program?
sections.html:
It is the city's process for auctioning property with long-delinquent real estate tax, and the city says it will relaunch in November 2026 after a pause that began in January 2023.

A property becomes eligible when taxes have been delinquent for two full calendar years, or one year if the property is condemned, a nuisance, derelict or blighted, under Virginia Code 58.1-3965. The city's example is that a bill due January 15, 2027 and left unpaid would become eligible for sale during 2029. The first sale is anticipated in the second half of 2027.

StageWhat the city describes
EligibilityCity Attorney reviews delinquent accounts
NoticeNotice of Intent mailed to owners and occupants
OptionsPayment plan, or redemption by paying taxes, penalties, interest and legal fees
AuctionSpecial Commissioner sells at public auction if unpaid

Properties are not eligible if they are unbuildable or if the owner is in bankruptcy. A payment arrangement can stop a sale while it stays in good standing, and the city limits owners to one tax type at a time and one new arrangement per 12 months (tax sale program).

sections.h2: Does Richmond offer real estate tax relief?
sections.html:
Yes. Finance runs the Older Adults and Persons with Disabilities Real Estate Tax Relief Program, and the Assessor runs an exemption for disabled veterans.

Both programs have separate applications, and the city's dates page lists a tax relief application and recertification deadline of December 31 on its real estate tab. A separate resident tab entry lists March 31 for relief applications and recertifications, so confirm which date applies to your program with Finance before you plan around either one.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Richmond tax when I sell the house?
sections.html:
The unpaid tax is paid from the sale proceeds, because Virginia gives real estate tax a lien ahead of any other lien.

The purchaser or foreclosure trustee must apply proceeds to taxes, which include penalties and interest, and the seller's share is prorated by contract (Va. Code 58.1-3340). The deed carries a state grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 of value, usually paid by the seller (Va. Code 58.1-802). Richmond's Circuit Court clerk handles deeds for the city.

  • Call Finance through RVA 311 for a payoff before you accept a closing date.
  • Ask whether the city has put the property into the tax sale program, since Finance takes no further collection action on accounts in that program.
  • Ask the closing agent to confirm that the lien release is recorded.

Sellers with back taxes, tenants or a house needing repairs often compare a direct sale with listing. In both cases the tax payoff comes out of the proceeds.

sections.h2: What other tax dates does Richmond publish for owners?
sections.html:
Richmond's important dates page lists several dates beyond the two real estate installments, and a few of them touch owners who rent a house out.

DateItem on the city list
January 1Value of real estate established
January 14Real estate tax, first half
January 20 and April 20Short-term rental property taxes, fourth and first quarter
June 5Personal property tax for vehicles, boats, trailers and motorcycles
June 14Real estate tax, second half

An owner who rents a Richmond home on a short-term basis should settle the quarterly rental tax before listing the house, so no old balance surprises the closing agent. The page does not say how those taxes are handled at a sale, so ask Finance through RVA 311.

faqs.q: When are Richmond real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: January 14 for the first half and June 14 for the second half, according to the city's important dates page.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Richmond assessment?
faqs.a: The Assessor of Real Estate at (804) 646-7500 or assessmentappeals@rva.gov. Billing questions go through RVA 311 at (804) 646-7000.

faqs.q: When does Richmond send reassessment notices?
faqs.a: On or about July 1 each year, according to the assessor's appeal page, with value as of July 1.

faqs.q: Can Richmond sell my house for unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, through its tax sale program, once taxes are delinquent for two full calendar years, or one year for condemned, derelict or blighted property. The city says it relaunches the program in November 2026.

faqs.q: Can I stop a Richmond tax sale?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Owners can redeem by paying taxes, penalties, interest and legal fees before the auction, or enter a payment plan. Call 311 to ask about your account.
